title: Normalized completed coefficient tensor presentation and its inverse image
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $h:S'\to S$ a morphism of schemes, and $H/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_H$ and uniformizer $\varpi_H$. Use the small pro-etale sites and their inverse image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $T=S,S'$ write $D_T=(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T$ and $B_{H,T}=(\mathcal O_H)_T$ for discrete constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and put
$$A_T=\varprojlim_r(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_T,\qquad R_{H,T}=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^n)_T$$
with $r,n\geq1$ and their projections [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\epsilon_T:D_T\to A_T$ send $a$ to its compatible residues. Let $\delta_C:h^{-1}C_S\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{S'}$ be the canonical comparison preserving constant sections, for each discrete ring $C$ [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. Let $\alpha_0:h^{-1}A_S\to A_{S'}$ and $\alpha_H:h^{-1}R_{H,S}\to R_{H,S'}$ be the projection-induced maps, using $\delta_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}$ and $\delta_{\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^n}$, respectively. All tensors below are sheafified balanced tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

There is a canonical isomorphism of ring sheaves
$$\beta_{H,T}:A_T\otimes_{D_T}B_{H,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{H,T}$$
whose $n$-th projection sends a local pure tensor $x\otimes b$ to $\mathrm{pr}_k(x)\bar b$ for any $k\geq1$ with $\ell^k\mathcal O_H\subseteq\varpi_H^n\mathcal O_H$. This formula is independent of $k$. The comparisons satisfy
$$\alpha_0h^{-1}\epsilon_S=\epsilon_{S'}\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell},\qquad
\alpha_Hh^{-1}\beta_{H,S}=\beta_{H,S'}(\alpha_0\otimes\delta_{\mathcal O_H})\sigma_h,$$
where $\sigma_h:h^{-1}(A_S\otimes_{D_S}B_{H,S})\xrightarrow{\sim}h^{-1}A_S\otimes_{h^{-1}D_S}h^{-1}B_{H,S}$ is the canonical tensor comparison, normalized by inverse images of pure tensors. Here $\delta_{\mathcal O_H}$ respects the $\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$-scalar structures.

For finite extensions $E\subset F$, write $q_{EF}:B_{E,T}\to B_{F,T}$ for the constant inclusion and $i_{EF}:R_{E,T}\to R_{F,T}$ for the map induced on limits by $\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^k\to\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ whenever $\varpi_E^k\mathcal O_F\subseteq\varpi_F^n\mathcal O_F$. Then
$$i_{EF}\beta_{E,T}=\beta_{F,T}(1\otimes q_{EF}),\qquad
\alpha_Fh^{-1}i_{EF}=i_{EF}\alpha_E,\qquad
\delta_{\mathcal O_F}h^{-1}q_{EF}=q_{EF}\delta_{\mathcal O_E}.$$
All displayed equalities are equalities of ring-sheaf maps, with the indicated inverse-image scalar identifications.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis] to $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq H$: choose a $\mathbf Z_\ell$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $\mathcal O_H$. By [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] the base valuation ring has uniformizer $\ell$ and $\mathbf Z_\ell/\ell^r=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$. By [lem-pur-local-field-coefficient-stages] there are $e\geq1$ and a unit $u$ with $\ell=u\varpi_H^e$, hence $\ell^r\mathcal O_H=\varpi_H^{er}\mathcal O_H$. These statements apply to arbitrary finite local-field extensions; no assumption on the characteristic or dimension of $T$ is involved.

source.place: Opening finite integral basis sentence; uniformizer arithmetic as in lem-pur-local-field-coefficient-stages

proof.text: Sheafify the mutually inverse additive coordinate maps $\mathbf Z_\ell^d\rightleftarrows\mathcal O_H$ and, for each $r$, their reductions $(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)^d\rightleftarrows\mathcal O_H/\ell^r\mathcal O_H$. Constant sheaves are sheafifications [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and sheafification preserves finite products via their projections [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact]. Thus these give $D_T$-linear isomorphisms $D_T^d\cong B_{H,T}$ and $((\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_T)^d\cong(\mathcal O_H/\ell^r\mathcal O_H)_T$, both with formula $(a_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_i b_i$. Linearity and the inverse identities are the sheafifications of the corresponding coordinate identities. The reduced isomorphisms commute with transition maps because reduction of $\sum_i a_i b_i$ is $\sum_i\bar a_i b_i$.

Use the compatible-tuple description of limits [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Restricting a tuple in $R_{H,T}$ to indices $er$ identifies it with $\lim_r(\mathcal O_H/\ell^r\mathcal O_H)_T$: the inverse sends $(z_r)_r$ to the tuple whose $n$-th entry is the reduction of $z_r$ for any $er\geq n$. Two choices agree after reduction from a common larger index; this also proves the two maps inverse. At every site object $U$, the coordinate maps of step 2 identify a compatible tuple $(z_r)_r$ with the $d$ compatible scalar tuples $(a_{i,r})_r$. The inverse takes these scalar tuples to $(\sum_i a_{i,r}b_i)_r$. These formulas commute with restriction in $U$ and prove an isomorphism $A_T^d\cong R_{H,T}$ of $D_T$-module sheaves.

The sheaf tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives $A_T\otimes_{D_T}B_{H,T}\cong A_T^d$ using the basis of step 2. Explicitly, if $q_i:B_{H,T}\to D_T$ are its coordinates, the maps are $x\otimes b\mapsto(x\epsilon_T(q_i(b)))_i$ and $(x_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i x_i\otimes b_i$. They are balanced maps on presheaf tensors and extend uniquely to sheafified tensors; the inverse identities follow from $b=\sum_i q_i(b)b_i$ and $q_i(b_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Composing with step 3 defines an additive sheaf isomorphism $\beta_{H,T}$. Its $er$-th projection is $(x\otimes b)\mapsto\operatorname{pr}_r(x)\bar b$. Reducing from a larger $er$ gives the formula at any $n$ and any $k$ with $ek\geq n$; a common larger $k$ proves independence. The ideal condition in the statement is exactly $ek\geq n$.

source.place: Section 03EK (section-tensor-product), tensor universal property and explicit basis maps

proof.text: Each projection of $\beta_{H,T}$ preserves multiplication and unit: for a common admissible $k$, the images of $(x\otimes b)(y\otimes c)=xy\otimes bc$ and of $(x\otimes b)(y\otimes c)$ computed after projection are both $\operatorname{pr}_k(x)\operatorname{pr}_k(y)\bar b\bar c$, and $1\otimes1$ maps to $1$. Bilinearity extends this equality to sums of pure tensors and the sheafification universal property extends it to the sheaf tensor. Projections jointly detect equality by [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Hence $\beta_{H,T}$ is a ring-sheaf map and its additive inverse is also multiplicative and unital (apply $\beta$ to the desired identities). Its normalized projections determine it uniquely, so the isomorphism is independent of the chosen integral basis.

proof.text: For every homomorphism of discrete coefficient rings $v:C\to C'$, prove $\delta_{C'}h^{-1}v_S=v_{S'}\delta_C$ as follows. The comparison $\delta_C$ is the constant-preserving isomorphism of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. Its adjoint is the map $\rho^h_C:C_S\to h_*C_{S'}$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], because that map extends the constant-presheaf map taking $c$ to the same constant $c$. The two adjoints in the desired equality both take $c$ to $v(c)$, and are therefore equal by the uniqueness in sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Apply this to $\mathbf Z_\ell\to\mathcal O_H$, to all residue maps, and to $q_{EF}$. This proves the required scalar compatibility and the displayed $\delta$-equation for $q_{EF}$.

Write $p_{H,n}$ and $p_{0,r}$ for the limit projections. By definition, $p'_{H,n}\alpha_H=\delta_{\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^n}h^{-1}p_{H,n}$ and $p'_{0,r}\alpha_0=\delta_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}h^{-1}p_{0,r}$; these cones define ring maps by [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Project the proposed $\epsilon$ equality to $r$. The left side is $\delta_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}h^{-1}(p_{0,r}\epsilon_S)$, whereas the right side is $(p'_{0,r}\epsilon_{S'})\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$. These are equal by step 6 for the residue homomorphism $\mathbf Z_\ell\to\mathbf Z/\ell^r$. Joint detection by projections gives $\alpha_0h^{-1}\epsilon_S=\epsilon_{S'}\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$.

proof.text: Let $\mu:A_S\times B_{H,S}\to A_S\otimes_{D_S}B_{H,S}$ be the universal $D_S$-balanced pairing [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Inverse image preserves finite products and carries the abelian, ring and module operations, with their identities, to those of $h^{-1}A_S,h^{-1}B_{H,S},h^{-1}D_S$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. So $h^{-1}\mu$, read on $h^{-1}A_S\times h^{-1}B_{H,S}\cong h^{-1}(A_S\times B_{H,S})$, is $h^{-1}D_S$-balanced and induces $\tau:h^{-1}A_S\otimes_{h^{-1}D_S}h^{-1}B_{H,S}\to h^{-1}(A_S\otimes_{D_S}B_{H,S})$ with $\tau(y\otimes c)=h^{-1}\mu(y,c)$, in particular $\tau(h^{-1}x\otimes h^{-1}b)=h^{-1}(x\otimes b)$. It is invertible: by steps 2 and 4, $(x_i)\mapsto\sum_ix_i\otimes b_i$ is an isomorphism $\gamma:A_S^d\cong A_S\otimes_{D_S}B_{H,S}$ and $D_S^d\cong B_{H,S}$ via the global sections $b_i$. Applying $h^{-1}$ gives $(h^{-1}D_S)^d\cong h^{-1}B_{H,S}$ with basis $h^{-1}b_i$, hence, by the computation of step 4 over $h^{-1}D_S$, an isomorphism $\gamma':(h^{-1}A_S)^d\cong h^{-1}A_S\otimes h^{-1}B_{H,S}$, $(y_i)\mapsto\sum_iy_i\otimes h^{-1}b_i$. On the $i$-th summand $h^{-1}\gamma$ is $h^{-1}$ of $x\mapsto\mu(x,b_i)$, that is $y\mapsto h^{-1}\mu(y,h^{-1}b_i)=\tau(y\otimes h^{-1}b_i)$; thus $\tau\gamma'=h^{-1}\gamma$ is invertible, so $\tau$ is. Put $\sigma_h=\tau^{-1}$; it is normalized as in the statement. It preserves multiplication and unit: $\mu(x,b)\mu(x',b')=\mu(xx',bb')$ and $\mu(1,1)=1$ are identities of sheaf maps, which $h^{-1}$ preserves. Step 7 makes $\alpha_0$ linear over $\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$, and step 6 does the same for $\delta_{\mathcal O_H}$, so $\alpha_0\otimes\delta_{\mathcal O_H}$ is defined.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), proof: the comparison corresponds to inverse-image balanced pairings; invertibility here from the finite basis of steps 2 and 4

proof.text: To prove the $\beta$ inverse-image square, fix $n$ and choose $k$ with $\ell^k\mathcal O_H\subseteq\varpi_H^n\mathcal O_H$. Denote the constant map $(\mathbf Z/\ell^k)_T\to(\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^n)_T$ by $j_T$ and $B_{H,T}\to(\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^n)_T$ by $v_T$. The $n$-th projection of $\beta$ is the balanced pairing $(x,b)\mapsto j_T(p_{0,k}(x))v_T(b)$. Apply $h^{-1}$ to this equality of pairings, and then the residue comparison $\delta_{\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^n}$. Step 6 replaces $h^{-1}j_S,h^{-1}v_S$ by $j_{S'},v_{S'}$ composed with the respective constant comparisons; step 7 replaces $\delta_{\mathbf Z/\ell^k}h^{-1}p_{0,k}$ by $p'_{0,k}\alpha_0$. Thus the resulting pairing is exactly the $n$-th projection of $\beta_{H,S'}(\alpha_0\otimes\delta_{\mathcal O_H})\sigma_h$. Equality of balanced pairings gives equality on tensor sheaves; joint detection by all $n$ gives the required ring-sheaf equation. This argument applies inverse image to morphisms and finite pairings, never to a limit comparison assumed invertible.

proof.text: For $E\subset F$, the uniformizer relation in [lem-pur-local-field-coefficient-stages] supplies admissible indices $a$ for every $n$. Let $j_{a,n}:(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^a)_T\to(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n)_T$ be the constant quotient map. The cone $j_{a,n}p_{E,a}$ is independent of $a$: compare two choices after increasing to a common larger index. Reduction in $n$ gives the cone defining $i_{EF}$ by [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Fix $n,a$ and choose $k$ with $\ell^k\mathcal O_E\subseteq\varpi_E^a\mathcal O_E$. Both $n$-th projections of $i_{EF}\beta_{E,T}$ and $\beta_{F,T}(1\otimes q_{EF})$ send $x\otimes b$ to $\operatorname{pr}_k(x)$ times the image of $b$ in $\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$. Hence they agree. Finally project the inverse-image $i$ equation to $n$: its left side becomes $\delta_{F,n}h^{-1}(j_{a,n}p_{E,a})$ and its right side becomes $j'_{a,n}\delta_{E,a}h^{-1}p_{E,a}$. Step 6 applied to $j_{a,n}$ identifies these maps. Tensor universal properties and joint detection by projections prove both displayed equalities. All maps involved preserve multiplication and unit, so these are equalities of ring-sheaf maps with exactly the stated scalar identifications.
